controls.title: Policies for information security
controls.description: Write an overall security policy plus supporting policies on specific topics, get leadership sign-off, make sure staff and relevant outside parties know and accept them, and revisit them regularly or after major changes.

controls.title: Information security roles and responsibilities
controls.description: Decide who owns each security duty in the organization, write those assignments down, and make sure every role knows what it is accountable for.

controls.title: Segregation of duties
controls.description: Split sensitive or conflicting tasks across different people so no single person can both perform and approve, or misuse, a critical activity unchecked.

controls.title: Management responsibilities
controls.description: Leaders should actively require everyone, including contractors, to follow the organization's security policies and procedures and back that expectation with visible support.

controls.title: Contact with authorities
controls.description: Keep up working relationships and current contact details for regulators, law enforcement and emergency services so you can reach them quickly when something happens.

controls.title: Contact with special interest groups
controls.description: Stay connected with security forums, industry groups and professional associations to share knowledge, get early warnings and keep skills current.

controls.title: Threat intelligence
controls.description: Gather information about threats relevant to your organization, analyze it, and use the results to adjust defenses and inform decisions.

controls.title: Information security in project management
controls.description: Build security into every project from the start, covering risks and requirements throughout planning, delivery and closure regardless of project type.

controls.title: Inventory of information and other associated assets
controls.description: Keep an up-to-date register of your information and the systems, devices and services that handle it, with a named owner for each item.

controls.title: Acceptable use of information and other associated assets
controls.description: Set clear rules for how people may use and handle information and related assets, document them, and put them into practice.

controls.title: Return of assets
controls.description: Make sure staff, contractors and other parties hand back every company asset in their possession when their job, contract or agreement ends or changes.

controls.title: Classification of information
controls.description: Sort information into sensitivity tiers, weighing how damaging disclosure, corruption or loss would be along with legal and stakeholder expectations, so protection matches its value.

controls.title: Labelling of information
controls.description: Create and apply a consistent way to mark information so its classification is obvious to anyone who handles it.

controls.title: Information transfer
controls.description: Put rules, procedures or agreements in place for moving information between people, systems or organizations, covering electronic, physical and verbal exchanges.

controls.title: Access control
controls.description: Define who may reach which information and systems, both logically and physically, based on business need and security requirements, and enforce it.

controls.title: Identity management
controls.description: Manage digital identities across their whole life, from creation to removal, so every account maps to a real person or system.

controls.title: Authentication information
controls.description: Control how passwords, keys and other secrets are issued and handled, and coach people on keeping their own credentials safe.

controls.title: Access rights
controls.description: Grant, review, change and revoke access permissions according to policy and business need, checking them periodically so they stay appropriate.

controls.title: Information security in supplier relationships
controls.description: Identify the security risks that come with using vendors' products and services and set up processes to manage them.

controls.title: Addressing information security within supplier agreements
controls.description: Write the relevant security expectations into each supplier contract, tailored to the kind of access or service that supplier provides.

controls.title: Managing information security in the ICT supply chain
controls.description: Manage security risks that flow through the technology supply chain, such as components, software and services sourced from upstream vendors.

controls.title: Monitoring, review and change management of supplier services
controls.description: Keep watch on how suppliers handle security and deliver services, review their performance regularly, and manage any changes they make.

controls.title: Information security for use of cloud services
controls.description: Set up processes for choosing, using, managing and leaving cloud services that reflect your own security needs and the shared responsibility model.

controls.title: Information security incident management planning and preparation
controls.description: Prepare for security incidents ahead of time by defining roles, procedures and communication paths for handling them.

controls.title: Assessment and decision on information security events
controls.description: Review reported security events and decide whether each one counts as an incident that needs a formal response.

controls.title: Response to information security incidents
controls.description: Respond to incidents using the documented procedures, containing damage and restoring normal operations.

controls.title: Learning from information security incidents
controls.description: After an incident, study what happened and feed the lessons back into controls so similar problems are less likely or less harmful.

controls.title: Collection of evidence
controls.description: Have procedures for identifying, gathering, preserving and handling evidence from security events so it holds up for disciplinary or legal use.

controls.title: Information security during disruption
controls.description: Plan how to keep information protected at an acceptable level while the business is dealing with a crisis or outage.

controls.title: ICT readiness for business continuity
controls.description: Make sure technology services can be restored and kept running to meet the recovery targets set by business continuity planning, and test that regularly.

controls.title: Legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements
controls.description: Identify every law, regulation and contractual obligation that touches information security, record them, and keep the list current along with your approach to meeting each.

controls.title: Intellectual property rights
controls.description: Put procedures in place to respect copyrights, licenses, patents and other intellectual property, including proper software licensing.

controls.title: Protection of records
controls.description: Guard business records against loss, tampering, destruction, unauthorized access or release, according to retention and legal needs.

controls.title: Privacy and protection of PII
controls.description: Know which privacy laws apply to personal data you handle, and put measures in place to protect that data and meet those obligations.

controls.title: Independent review of information security
controls.description: Have someone independent periodically assess how the organization manages security, and also after significant changes, covering people, process and technology.

controls.title: Compliance with policies, rules and standards for information security
controls.description: Check on a regular basis that teams actually follow the organization's security policies and standards, and fix gaps that turn up.

controls.title: Documented operating procedures
controls.description: Write down how to run information-processing facilities and tasks, and keep those procedures available to the people who need them.

controls.title: Screening
controls.description: Run background checks on job candidates before hiring and periodically afterward, proportionate to legal rules, the role and the information they'll see.

controls.title: Terms and conditions of employment
controls.description: Make security duties part of hiring agreements, so both the worker and the organization know what's expected around protecting information.

controls.title: Information security awareness, education and training
controls.description: Give staff and relevant outsiders ongoing security awareness and training suited to their roles, with regular updates on policies and procedures.

controls.title: Disciplinary process
controls.description: Have a formal, communicated process for dealing with people who break security policy.

controls.title: Responsibilities after termination or change of employment
controls.description: Spell out which confidentiality and security obligations continue after someone leaves or changes roles, tell them, and hold them to it.

controls.title: Confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements
controls.description: Use NDAs or confidentiality agreements that match what you need to protect, get employees and partners to sign them, and refresh the templates periodically.

controls.title: Remote working
controls.description: Apply extra safeguards for staff working from home or on the road, since company data they open or keep there sits outside your physical control.

controls.title: Information security event reporting
controls.description: Give people an easy, prompt way to report suspected or observed security events through the right channels.

controls.title: Physical security perimeters
controls.description: Draw clear physical boundaries around areas that hold sensitive information or systems and protect them appropriately.

controls.title: Physical entry
controls.description: Limit physical access to secure areas with entry controls and checkpoints so only authorized people get in.

controls.title: Securing offices, rooms and facilities
controls.description: Design and apply physical protections for offices, rooms and other facilities.

controls.title: Physical security monitoring
controls.description: Watch premises continuously, for example with alarms, guards or cameras, to detect unauthorized physical entry.

controls.title: Protecting against physical and environmental threats
controls.description: Plan and build protection against hazards such as fire, flood, earthquakes, storms and deliberate physical attacks on infrastructure.

controls.title: Working in secure areas
controls.description: Set rules and protective practices for anyone working inside secure areas.

controls.title: Clear desk and clear screen
controls.description: Require clear desks of papers and removable media, and lock or clear screens when unattended, enforcing it consistently.

controls.title: Equipment siting and protection
controls.description: Place and protect equipment carefully to reduce physical and environmental risks and opportunities for unauthorized access.

controls.title: Security of assets off-premises
controls.description: Protect devices and data that leave the office, keeping in mind the added risks of working outside company premises.

controls.title: Storage media
controls.description: Manage storage media throughout its life, from acquisition and use through transport and disposal, in line with classification and handling rules.

controls.title: Supporting utilities
controls.description: Shield server rooms and other technology facilities from outages in electricity, cooling, water, telecoms and similar services they depend on, for example with UPS units and generators.

controls.title: Cabling security
controls.description: Route and shield power and network cabling so it can't easily be tapped, disrupted or physically damaged.

controls.title: Equipment maintenance
controls.description: Service equipment properly so it stays available, reliable and secure, and so information isn't exposed during maintenance.

controls.title: Secure disposal or re-use of equipment
controls.description: Before throwing away or repurposing any device with storage, confirm that sensitive data and licensed software have been wiped or overwritten so nothing can be recovered.

controls.title: User endpoint devices
controls.description: Secure laptops, phones and other endpoints so the information they store, process or reach is protected.

controls.title: Privileged access rights
controls.description: Tightly restrict and closely manage who receives administrator or other elevated privileges and how they are used.

controls.title: Information access restriction
controls.description: Limit who can get to information and application functions according to the access control policy.

controls.title: Access to source code
controls.description: Limit who can view or modify code repositories, development tooling and shared libraries, so the codebase stays protected from tampering and leaks.

controls.title: Secure authentication
controls.description: Use strong, appropriate login technologies and procedures, such as MFA, matched to the sensitivity of the systems and access involved.

controls.title: Capacity management
controls.description: Track how resources are used today and forecast future needs so systems keep enough capacity.

controls.title: Protection against malware
controls.description: Defend against malware with technical tools backed by user awareness.

controls.title: Management of technical vulnerabilities
controls.description: Find out about technical weaknesses in your systems quickly, judge how exposed you are, and take timely action such as patching.

controls.title: Configuration management
controls.description: Set secure baseline settings for hardware, software, services and networks, record them, roll them out, and check over time that systems haven't drifted from them.

controls.title: Information deletion
controls.description: Remove data from systems, devices and storage once it is no longer needed.

controls.title: Data masking
controls.description: Hide or obscure sensitive data, for example through masking, pseudonymization or anonymization, in line with access policy, business needs and legal rules.

controls.title: Data leakage prevention
controls.description: Apply controls to systems, networks and devices that handle sensitive data to spot and stop unauthorized leaks or exfiltration.

controls.title: Information backup
controls.description: Take backups of data, software and systems per an agreed backup policy and test restoring them regularly.

controls.title: Redundancy of information processing facilities
controls.description: Build enough redundancy into processing facilities to meet the organization's availability needs.

controls.title: Logging
controls.description: Capture user actions, errors, failures and other security-relevant events in logs, keep those logs safe from tampering, and review them.

controls.title: Monitoring activities
controls.description: Watch for unusual activity across your infrastructure and applications, and investigate anything suspicious to determine whether it is an incident.

controls.title: Clock synchronization
controls.description: Keep the clocks on all systems synced to an approved time source so logs and events line up.

controls.title: Use of privileged utility programs
controls.description: Tightly limit and supervise tools that can bypass normal system or application safeguards, such as admin utilities.

controls.title: Installation of software on operational systems
controls.description: Use controlled procedures and measures for putting software onto production systems.

controls.title: Networks security
controls.description: Harden and administer your networks and network equipment so the systems and data riding on them stay protected.

controls.title: Security of network services
controls.description: Spell out the security features and service levels you need from network services, whether in-house or outsourced, put them in place and keep checking they're delivered.

controls.title: Segregation of networks
controls.description: Split the network into separate zones for different groups of services, users and systems.

controls.title: Web filtering
controls.description: Filter or block risky websites so people are less likely to land on malicious content while browsing.

controls.title: Use of cryptography
controls.description: Set and follow rules for using encryption properly, including how cryptographic keys are managed.

controls.title: Secure development life cycle
controls.description: Set rules for building software and systems securely across the full development lifecycle.

controls.title: Application security requirements
controls.description: Identify, specify and approve security needs before developing or buying applications.

controls.title: Secure system architecture and engineering principles
controls.description: Establish, document, maintain and apply sound security engineering principles whenever systems are designed or built.

controls.title: Secure coding
controls.description: Follow secure coding practices when writing software so code has fewer exploitable flaws.

controls.title: Security testing in development and acceptance
controls.description: Define and run security tests during development and before accepting systems into production.

controls.title: Outsourced development
controls.description: When outsiders build software or systems for you, steer and oversee their work and check it meets your security requirements.

controls.title: Separation of development, test and production environments
controls.description: Keep dev, test and live environments apart and protect each one.

controls.title: Change management
controls.description: Run changes to systems and processing facilities through a formal change control process.

controls.title: Test information
controls.description: Choose test data carefully and protect and manage it, avoiding unprotected use of real sensitive data.

controls.title: Protection of information systems during audit testing
controls.description: Plan audits and other assessments of live systems jointly with management so testing doesn't disrupt operations.
